notes: Brigade-level (below stated scope; included for context). Churchill tanks attached to VIII Corps for Epsom supporting 15th Division. current_activity: with the 4th Armoured Brigade, supports the VIII Corps infantry on the eastern flank of the Odon corridor
notes: Event date: 27 June 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 280). Event definition: On the second day of Operation Epsom tanks of the brigade and of the 4th Armoured Brigade, which have been supporting the VIII Corps infantry and feeling for the enemy on the eastern flank, are stationed for the night in positions to resist an attack from either flank (p. 280); on the first day the brigade had supported the 44th and 46th Brigades of the 15th Division behind a moving barrage (p. 277). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 280: "Tanks of the 31st Tank Brigade and of the 4th Armoured Brigade had been supporting the VIII Corps infantry and feeling for the enemy on the eastern flank"; p. 277: "they set off behind a strong moving barrage and were supported by the 31st Tank Brigade". Location: the dataset place Cheux sector with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the Cheux sector in the corridor. Location support: Ellis puts the brigade on the eastern flank of the corridor (p. 280).

current_activity: leaves the independent brigades: transferred to the 79th Armoured Division to become a Crocodile flame-tank brigade
notes: Event date: 4 September 1944 (Wikipedia, 31st Armoured Brigade); Ellis lists the last regiments leaving to 31 August (vol. I, p. 522). Event definition: After its regiments are detached to convert to the Churchill Crocodile flame-thrower (the 7th Royal Tank Regiment to 17 August, the 9th to 31 August, the 144th Regiment R.A.C. from 23 to 31 August, Ellis, p. 522), the brigade is transferred to the 79th Armoured Division on 4 September (Wikipedia); it then serves as a component of that division, so its independent period ends. Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 522: "7th Battalion R.T.R. (to 17.8.44)"; Wikipedia, 31st Armoured Brigade (United Kingdom): "on 4 September, the brigade was transferred to the 79th Armoured Division". Location: the dataset place Caen sector (representative point) with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: a representative point; the brigade headquarters is not placed by the sources read. Location support: no source read places the brigade headquarters on the day. Context: Correction to the planning list: the list gave June to August 1944; the brigade arrived in France on 19 June (Wikipedia) and its independent period ends on 4 September 1944. Later rows, as a component of the 79th Armoured Division, are out of scope for this batch.
